items.title: Anthropic details infrastructure hardening after cyber incidents
items.summary_en: Anthropic published an update describing changes made after security incidents earlier in the year, including a paused-then-resumed external and internal cyber-evaluation program, a new real-time classifier, migrated sandboxes, and a rebuilt RL-training-environment pipeline. Concrete changes cited include reducing standing access to systems holding model weights or customer data, defaulting to block outbound cluster traffic, and requiring verified internal service identity between systems.
items.notes: Blog post URL slug inferred from newsroom listing title 'Improving our alignment and security efforts'; content verified via search summaries of the official post, not directly fetched by this collector.

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1
items.summary_en: Anthropic introduced Fable 5.1 (generally available, standard safeguards) and Mythos 5.1 (restricted-access, for vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations) as the same underlying model shipped in two safeguard tiers. Anthropic cut Fable 5.1's cache-hit input pricing sharply versus Fable 5. Anthropic highlighted example outputs, including a high-resolution partial elevation map of Venus from NASA Magellan radar data and GPU-kernel optimizations that sped up several open-source deep learning models.
items.notes: Confirmed listed in official newsroom index with this URL and date.

items.title: Anthropic previews Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, developed with over 100 customers
items.summary_en: Anthropic described Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), which combines zero data retention with misuse-detection systems: customer interaction data is stored in cloud infrastructure the customer controls (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage) and encrypted with customer-held keys, while automated systems scan a rolling window of traffic for signs of serious misuse such as offensive cyber or biological capability development or stolen credentials. Anthropic said EFS was built with more than 100 customers across finance, healthcare, manufacturing and other sectors and cloud partners AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, and will roll out in phases starting later this fall.

items.title: Anthropic publishes September 2026 threat intelligence report on Claude misuse
items.summary_en: Anthropic released a report covering eight months (December 2025-August 2026) of disrupted attempts to misuse Claude across seven harm areas: cyber operations, influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud, biological misuse, conventional weapons development, and distillation. The report describes AI narrowing the gap between resource-rich state actors and individuals, including a case in which a suspected Russian espionage group used AI agents to iteratively rebuild malware until it evaded detection, and another describing a Russian-linked campaign (tracked as GTG-20006 / Midnight Blizzard) that targeted Ukrainian government, defense, and drone-supply-chain organizations over about 130 days.
items.notes: Listed in official newsroom index as 'Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026'.

items.title: Anthropic opens applications for Life Sciences Verification Program
items.summary_en: Anthropic opened applications for its Life Sciences Verification Program (LSVP), which gives vetted life-science professionals access to Anthropic models, including Mythos for the first time, under a modified safeguard set intended to allow biology-related work such as drug discovery, research biology, clinical development and manufacturing that is otherwise restricted in generally available Fable models. Applicants undergo a review of research credentials, security standards and ethical oversight, and can apply for 'Standard Use' or 'High-risk Use' access grants; the program is currently open to Claude Enterprise, Team and API customers, not individual Pro/Max users.

items.title: Anthropic discloses internal 'R&D Automation Index' measuring Claude's role in its own research
items.summary_en: Anthropic published measurements of how much of its internal model research and development is handled by Claude, using a six-level automation scale (AL0-AL5) developed by Epoch AI. Anthropic reported that Claude 'leads' (completes most of a task end-to-end from a high-level prompt, under human supervision) 26% of measured R&D work as of August 2026, up from under 1% in February, and that over 90% of R&D work reaches at least 'AI collaborates' status. Anthropic said no measured R&D subset has reached full autonomy (AL5), and that roughly 30,000 agents were running simultaneously on its internal research platform with monitoring in place.
items.notes: Published date is approximate: the page's own timestamp was ambiguous when checked, but multiple independent news reports (Forkast, BetaNews, Quartz) converge on Sept 17-18, 2026 as the disclosure date.

items.title: Anthropic partners with Accenture on embedded third-party evaluation
items.summary_en: Anthropic announced a partnership with Accenture (led by Accenture's Faculty AI business) to provide independent evaluation of Anthropic's frontier models, including red-teaming, alignment assessments and safeguard testing. Anthropic said it will fund Accenture's work directly, describing the move as a step toward embedding evaluators inside the company, a commitment made in an earlier essay by Anthropic's CEO titled 'We Must Pace the Frontier.' Anthropic and Accenture said they expect to invest at least $1 billion combined in this evaluation capacity over five years.

items.title: Anthropic describes Claude's use in DRC Ebola outbreak response
items.summary_en: Anthropic published a feature describing how WHO's African regional office and partners are using Claude to help respond to a Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Described uses include compiling daily situation reports from health-worker data (cutting compilation time from a full day to under an hour), running multiple outbreak forecasting models in parallel to guide treatment-center placement, organizing vaccine-development proposal data for faster expert review, and using Claude Science to assemble viral genomes from sequencing fragments and build phylogenetic trees.
items.notes: Listed as 'The Situation Report' in newsroom index with a Sept 22 display date, but the article's own byline date reads Sept 19, 2026; both fall within the collection window.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary_en: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in a new 5.5 family, which it said performs at roughly the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work with a 1-million-token context window, while costing about 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads (API list prices: $4/million input tokens, $20/million output tokens, $0.20/million cache reads). Anthropic said the model scored strongest to date on its automated behavioral safety audit and was tested pre-release by external evaluators including Frontier Design and METR. The release includes an anti-distillation safeguard called 'preserved thinking' that blocks API users from editing Claude's prior reasoning context to extract it, and communication changes making Opus less likely to use jargon. Anthropic said Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 will follow in coming weeks.
items.notes: Confirmed in official newsroom index. Cross-reference: METR's own predeployment evaluation summary of this model is a separate item in this week's METR collector file.

items.title: Anthropic's life sciences lab reports Claude-assisted discovery of a novel enzyme system
items.summary_en: Anthropic said its newly formed life sciences research group used Claude agents to identify a previously uncharacterized enzyme system in bacteriophages, termed 'array-associated reverse transcriptases' (ART), which pairs a reverse transcriptase with DNA repeat arrays structurally similar to CRISPR. Anthropic said roughly 950 Claude agents searched DNA sequence databases over 21 hours (about 210 million tokens), narrowing an initial pool of over 200,000 candidate reverse transcriptases down to about 20, a process Anthropic said typically takes human scientists weeks to months. CRISPR co-discoverer Feng Zhang (MIT) was quoted giving a brief positive assessment of the approach. Anthropic said its Bay Area lab conducts only biosafety level 1-2 work, with human scientists performing all wet-lab experiments while Claude assists with analysis.
items.notes: Directly fetched and confirmed by this collector.

items.title: Claude Code on the web reaches general availability
items.summary_en: Anthropic updated its Claude Code on the web post (rebranded as 'Cloud sessions') to announce the feature's move from research preview to general availability. It lets developers delegate coding tasks to Claude running on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure, supports running multiple tasks in parallel across repositories in isolated sandboxes, integrates with GitHub for automatic pull-request creation, offers real-time progress monitoring, and includes early iOS mobile access. Anthropic said network and filesystem restrictions and a secure Git proxy limit repository access for security.
items.notes: This is an update to a post originally published in an earlier product cycle (research preview announcement); the Sept 23, 2026 date marks the GA status-change update, not a first announcement. Flagging so the synthesis agent does not treat this as a brand-new feature.

coverage_note: Full official newsroom coverage for the 2026-08-29 to 2026-09-26 window was retrieved and cross-checked against anthropic.com/news. Two widely-reported items — a 'Claude for Financial Advisors' product (reported ~Sept 14, 2026 by Bloomberg/AdvisorHub) and a Novo Nordisk drug-discovery collaboration (reported ~Sept 16-17, 2026 by Bloomberg/BioSpace) — were excluded from this file because no official Anthropic blog/newsroom URL could be located for either (direct URL guesses returned 404 and neither appears in the current newsroom index); per collection rules only official sources are permitted, so these are flagged here rather than cited to press coverage. Items published on or before 2026-08-27 (e.g. Model Hardware Standard preview, Expanding support for scientists, Fable 5 biology safeguards update, text-watermark explainer, wellbeing-evaluation funding) were excluded as out-of-window, since the prior run date was 2026-08-29 and those items would already have been eligible for capture then.
